label:
Milk caramel
(and fudge)
step: cook with sugar and fat to a set stage
note: At the firm-ball stage (120 °C) the sugar itself is too cool to caramelise, so this is called milk or cream caramel: the milk browns. Fudge is cooked to the soft-ball stage and beaten so that it crystallises.

about.text: A chewy sweet cooked from milk or cream, sugar, glucose syrup and butter; sold as milk caramels or cream caramels.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Cream and butter are stirred into hot sugar syrup, which is cooked again to the firm-ball stage; vanilla and salt go in last (vanilla earlier would burn off, salt earlier would invert the sugar).

steps.note: Sugar and glucose are heated to 130 °C, then cream and butter are added.
Cooked again to the firm-ball stage; vanilla and salt go in last.
